title: Unifying multimodal understanding and generation
reading: The slide presents MetaMorph (Tong et al., 2024) as an example of unifying multimodal understanding and generation: a single autoregressive model that can emit both text and visual tokens. A three-panel figure from the paper illustrates the VPiT training setup, the inference pipeline, and qualitative examples; the citation appears at the bottom.

visuals.description: Three panels. Left, 'VPiT': text and image inputs go through a frozen vision encoder plus trainable adapter into a trainable Autoregressive Model with trainable Text Head and Vision Head (flame icons mark trainable parts, snowflake marks frozen). Middle, 'Inference': text/image inputs via adapter and encoder into the Autoregressive Model, whose Text Head emits text and Vision Head emits visual tokens that pass through a Projector into an Adapted Diffusion Model producing an image. Right, 'Examples': a chat where the user asks to generate the animal resulting from a monarch caterpillar's metamorphosis, the model returns a butterfly image with <image_start><image_end> tokens, and then correctly answers that the animal is a butterfly.
visuals.assertion: Instruction tuning on visual prediction (VPiT) lets one autoregressive backbone predict both text and continuous visual tokens, which a separately adapted diffusion model decodes into images, supporting both generation and understanding in one conversation.

concepts.name: VPiT (Visual Predictive Instruction Tuning)
concepts.why_it_matters: Training recipe that gives an LLM the ability to predict visual tokens.

concepts.name: Unified autoregressive multimodal model
concepts.why_it_matters: Single model handles both understanding and generation instead of separate systems.

concepts.name: Adapted diffusion model as visual decoder
concepts.why_it_matters: Converts predicted visual tokens into actual pixels.
